how_to_read_for_egret: raw_records and findings are EVIDENCE of what Kestra did. egret_expected holds the values later tasks deserialize (Tasks 3-12); egret_expected_basis says how each key was obtained: measured (on the artifact), code (a class of the artifact run in jshell, or egret source), schema (plugin JSON schema), chosen (the spec's answer where Kestra's cannot be measured or egret differs on purpose). Rendered values of file functions are the strings a Return task's `format` produced. Log messages longer than 700 chars are truncated and marked; no finding quotes a truncated part.

findings.finding: GET /api/v1/plugins lists io.kestra.plugin.core (with core.storage.{Concat, DeduplicateItems, Delete, FilterItems, PurgeCurrentExecutionFiles, PurgeStorage, Reverse, Size, Split, Write} and core.flow.Loop) and the three JDBC groups io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.{postgresql, mysql, trino} at 2.0.0 (each twice: bundled + mounted). The image did not refuse the jars.

An outputFiles match is stored as tasks/{task-slug}/{taskRunId}/{IdUtils.from(<absolute path>)}-{file name with ' ' -> '+'}: 'a b.txt' at /tmp/kestra-wd/tmp/2Aq5usxbinvaJ4FOgvRtMW/a b.txt -> '4Oo1ozB6Q4i9blmqxJeRKY-a+b.txt'. IdUtils.from of exactly that absolute path (spaces kept) gives 4Oo1ozB6Q4i9blmqxJeRKY in jshell; the same holds for sub/x.csv, one.log, two.log. The key in outputs.outputFiles is the path relative to the working directory ('sub/x.csv'); the URI keeps only the file name ('…-x.csv'), not the sub-directory.
IdUtils.from returns 21- or 22-character ids (e.g. 'ivSfsPLqY0bFp5gRNFxm0' is 21, 'nyvijVmYrUyvm5NPilx5H' observed in a file name is 21): FriendlyId is not zero-padded.

Namespace dots become '/' (w9a.storage -> w9a/storage); flow and task ids are slugified: 'Out_Files.Case-' -> 'out-filescase' ('.' removed, '_' -> '-', trailing '-' dropped, lower-cased), 'Shell_Task-' -> 'shell-task'. Slugify.of drops every non-ASCII-word character after NFD (so '中文' -> '' and 'ﬁ ligature' -> 'ligature': NFD does not decompose the ligature).

core.storage.Write names its file {random unsigned decimal}{extension}; with no `extension` the extension is '.tmp' (Write_NoExt -> 7709222568156811597.tmp). Concat (default .tmp), Split, Reverse, DeduplicateItems, FilterItems and the JDBC STORE files are named the same way. postgresql.CopyOut names its file 'copy-out' (no extension).

outputDirectory: true exposes the directory as the render variable outputDir and the env var OUTPUT_DIR, both '/tmp/kestra-wd/tmp/2Aq5usxbinvaJ4FOgvRtMW/5CTBQ7UCQeSZrt5n4BxRIP' — a fresh random id under the working directory. Its files are keyed by their path relative to it ('od.txt', 'deep/d.txt') and stored under that relative path verbatim (no hash).

An inputFiles value that renders to a kestra:// URI is downloaded into the working directory under the key ('staged.txt', 'd/nested.txt' with the sub-directory created); the task reads the contents. A non-URI value is written as contents. The task's outputs carry no trace of the URI.

Kestra 2.0 (this artifact) runs each Loop iteration as a sub-execution of kind LOOP, linked to the root by the label system.correlationId. Inside the iteration `execution.id` renders the ROOT id (2G1i2hGvCOdQ5cwWChXwwu), but a file the iteration writes carries the ITERATION's id: kestra:///w9a/storage/ff-main/executions/77sQ6gKNV9aTzN13CRo7lw/tasks/iter-write/5VOEu37QYyacAafxgBUFin/13731611245591839406.txt. GET /executions/<root>/file?path=<that uri> answers 301 to /executions/<iteration>/file; via the iteration id it answers 200. This contradicts spec §3's 'Kestra runs it inside the one execution … so its URI is the one Kestra would give' (amended).

loop-outputs-auto: Loop `outputs` with values from a URI (AUTO -> STORE) writes one Ion file per iteration at kestra:///{ns}/{flow}/executions/{ITERATION id}/{random}.ion — a tail with no inputs/, tasks/ or trigger/ segment — holding {value:"some output"}; `end` renders those URIs. The golden entry compares states and values only.

In OSS every case that names an existing file answers a value: own, the loop root from an iteration, the Subflow parent, the Flow-trigger source and an UNRELATED execution of the same namespace (read 'unrelated content'). egret refuses the last by design (spec §2, §4.4).

fileExists on a well-formed URI of the running execution that names no file answers false; read, fileSize and isFileEmpty on it fail with 'File not found for URI: <uri>'. A URI that does not match the execution-file layout fails all four ('Unable to read the file '<uri>' as it is not an execution file'), as do '..' ('File should be accessed with their full path and not using relative '..' path.') and another scheme ('Cannot process the URI s3://bucket/key.txt: scheme not supported.').

read() of the bytes ff fe 00 81 rendered three U+FFFD characters and no error: decoding is lossy, not refused. The NUL byte is absent from the recorded value; whether read() or the artifact's Postgres-backed output storage dropped it cannot be told apart from this measurement.

A FILE input arrives as a multipart part named by the input id; its URI is kestra:///{ns}/{flow}/executions/{id}/inputs/{input}/{filename}. allowedFileExtensions: ['.txt'] did NOT refuse 'bad.csv' on the artifact — neither at start (200, SUCCESS) nor via POST …/validate (errors: []); the refusal text exists only in source (FileInput.validate). A file name with a space is refused 422 (URISyntaxException); '%20', '+' and accents are kept verbatim. A text part holding a kestra:// URI of another execution is accepted verbatim and read at run; a non-URI string is 422 'Invalid value for input `f`. Cause: Illegal character in path at index 3: not a uri'.

/file answers 200 application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>"; filename*=utf-8''<pct-encoded name>, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, chunked. /file/metas answers {"size": n}. /file/preview answers {extension, type, content, truncated}: .ion/.csv/.jsonl are type LIST of rows (csv values as strings), .txt/.json/.bin/no extension are type TEXT; maxRows=2 sets truncated true; maxRows above the max is clamped (5000 per the controller). In ION preview rows a null field is OMITTED, a timestamp is its Ion text as a string, a decimal a JSON number (12.50 -> 12.5, 1d2 -> 100.0). A URI of another execution is 301 with Location /api/v1/main/executions/<owner>/file?path=<uri>; a missing file 404 'File not found for URI: <uri>'; '..' 422.

Every JDBC STORE file (postgres, trino, mysql/StarRocks), and DeduplicateItems/FilterItems output, is BINARY Ion 1.0, each row preceded by its own version marker e0 01 00 ea and local symbol table. Decoded by the artifact's ion-java: a timestamp is the annotated string LocalDateTime::"2026-01-02T03:04:05.123456", a timestamptz ZonedDateTime::"2026-01-01T20:04:05Z[Etc/UTC]" (converted to UTC), a date an Ion timestamp 2026-01-02, a decimal keeps its scale (12.340), bytea a blob, NULL a null field. egret's runners::ionfmt writes Ion TEXT; the bytes cannot match.

STORE output keys are {uri, size}; size counts rows (0 rows -> size 0 and a 0-byte file). The file name is random per run (two runs: 3654590194353406031.ion / 1449160271353627895.ion), extension .ion. So egret's STORE uses a deterministic name (spec §9.2 amended).

postgresql.CopyOut, CopyIn, Batch (sql and table forms), mysql.Batch (StarRocks), every Query/Queries STORE and store: true ran their storage part on the artifact. mysql.Query/Queries inputFile staged the file at <working dir>/inputFile and StarRocks refused the LOAD DATA statement itself. still_refused_values is {}.

One run each (bytes in egret_expected.core_storage): Concat joins with no separator by default, with `separator` appended AFTER every file including the last; Split rows:2 -> [l1 l2][l3 l4][l5], partitions:2 -> round-robin [l1 l3 l5][l2 l4], bytes:'6' -> [l1 l2][l3 l4][l5]; Size -> bytes; Reverse reverses lines keeping the trailing newline; DeduplicateItems keeps the LAST item per key, in the order of those last items (b, a(v=3), c); FilterItems INCLUDE v>1 drops one, EXCLUDE k=='a' drops two; Delete -> {uri, deleted:true}, again {deleted:false}, errorOnMissing:true fails 'Unable to find file '<uri>''; PurgeCurrentExecutionFiles -> {uris: [every file AND every directory prefix it removed, deepest first, ending at the execution prefix]}. In OSS Size and Delete also act on ANOTHER execution's file (Delete removed it).

A Loop over an Ion file makes one iteration per top-level value; item.value is: a string as itself, a number's Ion text (12.50 stays '12.50'), anything else JSON (a struct, a list, `true`, and a timestamp as the JSON string "2025-12-03T12:00:00.000000Z" WITH quotes). A null value fails the Loop with 'Found a null value in the ION file' after the iterations before it were started (1 of 3 ran).
egret's Trino and StarRocks connectors read incrementally from the wire but collect every row (up to max_rows) into a Vec before returning one TabularResult; nothing streams through QueryExecPort.

Not measured: a file with a space inside outputDirectory; Kestra's fileExists on a URI of another tenant (OSS has one); preview max clamp value (the controller's previewMaxRows; maxRows=99999 returned all 3 rows, which neither confirms nor refutes 5000).

sr_storage.flow_yaml:
id: sr_storage
namespace: w9a.plugins
tasks:
  - id: setup_db
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS w9a"
  - id: setup_drop
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS w9a.t"
  - id: setup_create
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "CREATE TABLE w9a.t (i INT, t VARCHAR(20)) DUPLICATE KEY(i) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(i) BUCKETS 1 PROPERTIES ('replication_num' = '1')"
  - id: ion
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.storage.Write
    extension: .ion
    content: |
      {i:20,t:"p"}
      {i:21,t:"q"}
      {i:22,t:null}
  - id: batch
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Batch
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    from: "{{ outputs.ion.uri }}"
    sql: "INSERT INTO w9a.t (i, t) VALUES (?, ?)"
  - id: check
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "SELECT i, t FROM w9a.t ORDER BY i"
    fetchType: FETCH
  - id: q_store
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "SELECT i, t FROM w9a.t ORDER BY i"
    fetchType: STORE
  - id: q_store_true
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    sql: "SELECT 1 AS a"
    store: true
  - id: qs_store
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Queries
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    allowFailure: true
    sql: "SELECT 1 AS a; SELECT 2 AS b"
    fetchType: STORE
  - id: qs_store_one
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Queries
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    allowFailure: true
    sql: "SELECT 1 AS a"
    fetchType: STORE
  - id: csv
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.storage.Write
    extension: .csv
    content: |
      30,x
      31,y
  - id: q_inputfile
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    allowFailure: true
    inputFile: "{{ outputs.csv.uri }}"
    sql: "LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '{{ inputFile }}' INTO TABLE w9a.t FIELDS TERMINATED BY ','"
  - id: qs_inputfile
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Queries
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/
    username: root
    allowFailure: true
    inputFile: "{{ outputs.csv.uri }}"
    sql: "LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '{{ inputFile }}' INTO TABLE w9a.t FIELDS TERMINATED BY ','"
  - id: check_after
    type: io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query
    url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/

    sql: "SELECT i, t FROM w9a.t ORDER BY i"
    fetchType: FETCH
